title: Learning Multi-Objective Rewards and User Utility Function in Contextual Bandits for Personalized Ranking
abstract: Uses contextual bandits to learn multiple ranking objectives together with user-specific utility weights. It is transfer evidence for adaptive multi-objective personalization, but its utility optimization does not independently distinguish mandatory workplace obligations from soft preferences.

title: Conflicting information integration for decision support
abstract: Examines methods for integrating conflicting information from multiple sources for decision-support purposes and proposes an information-theoretic treatment. It is mechanism-level evidence for handling disputed multi-source state rather than an experiment on workplace briefing presentation.

title: What Did I Ask You to Do, by When, and for Whom?: Passion and Compassion in Request Management
abstract: Studies workplace request management when requests are scattered across communication channels. It reports difficulties with aggregation, prioritization, context, deadlines, and accountability and derives design implications for tools that maintain actionable requests.

title: Agent Newsroom: Efficient Chronological Report Generation via Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration
abstract: Generates chronological reports from evolving document streams using dynamically coordinated agents for coverage and diversity, cross-review to reduce redundancy, duplicate adjudication, and adaptive control. It provides recent transfer evidence for repeated-cycle report generation under evolving input, but not explicit workplace obligation states.

title: Requests and Commitments in Email are More Complex Than You Think: Eight Reasons to be Cautious
abstract: Analyzes difficult cases in identifying requests and commitments in workplace email and documents several sources of ambiguity. It offers annotation and modeling guidance for obligation-oriented email processing.

title: The Learning Behind Gmail Priority Inbox
abstract: Describes the machine-learning system behind Gmail Priority Inbox, including per-user models that are updated frequently from user behavior. The system is relevant to adaptive personalized ranking, while its targets concern user actions rather than independently labeled workplace obligations.
venue: NIPS Workshop on Learning on Cores, Clusters and Clouds

title: Exploiting relevance, coverage, and novelty for query-focused multi-document summarization
abstract: Presents a query-focused multi-document summarization framework that jointly models relevance to the information need, content coverage, and novelty. It provides transfer mechanisms for balancing omission and repetition but is a static summarization setting rather than a repeated workplace briefing cycle.

title: The Nature of Requests and Commitments in Email Messages
abstract: Develops precise utterance-level definitions for requests and commitments in workplace email and applies them to Enron messages. The work is directly relevant to distinguishing responsibility-bearing requests and promises from generic importance or likely user actions.

title: Can requests-for-action and commitments-to-act be reliably identified in email messages?
abstract: Investigates whether requests for action and commitments to act can be annotated reliably in workplace email. It provides direct evidence that obligation-related speech acts can be treated as distinct annotation targets rather than inferred from response probability or generic importance.

title: Smart To-Do: Automatic Generation of To-Do Items from Emails
abstract: Introduces automatic generation of concise to-do items from emails in which a sender has committed to an action. The task provides a mechanism for turning commitment-bearing email content into explicit work items, although it does not evaluate longitudinal work-item state transitions.

title: Adaptive User Modeling with Long and Short-Term Preferences for Personalized Recommendation
abstract: Models both long-term and short-term user preferences and adaptively combines them using time- and content-aware mechanisms. It is transfer evidence for personalization that changes with user behavior rather than remaining a fixed profile.

title: Scaling up Ranking under Constraints for Live Recommendations by Replacing Optimization with Prediction
abstract: Studies real-time ranking subject to explicit constraints and approximates an optimization-based constrained-ranking solution with a predictive model. The work is transferable to architectures that enforce hard briefing requirements separately from utility-oriented ranking.

title: Beyond SumBasic: Task-focused summarization with sentence simplification and lexical expansion
abstract: Develops task-focused multi-document summarization intended to answer a specified information need, combining content selection with sentence simplification and lexical expansion. It supplies foundational transfer evidence for requirement-directed briefing selection but has no longitudinal accepted-view state.

title: Timeline Generation through Evolutionary Trans-Temporal Summarization
abstract: Generates timelines from time-stamped document collections using summaries that are related across dates. The method models temporal evolution and cross-date content selection, but does not explicitly represent persistent open, resolved, revoked, or superseded work-item states.

title: Effects of visualizing uncertainty on decision-making in a target identification scenario
abstract: Evaluates decision making under time pressure with and without explicit uncertainty visualization in a target-identification and prioritization setting. The study measures how uncertainty displays affect operators' decisions, priorities, and behavior rather than only subjective visualization preference.

title: QMSum: A New Benchmark for Query-based Multi-domain Meeting Summarization
abstract: Introduces query-based summarization of long meetings, including queries concerning decisions and tasks, and evaluates locate-then-summarize approaches. It is relevant to decision- and action-focused content selection but does not by itself establish cross-conversation incremental work-item tracking.

title: A survey on concept drift adaptation
abstract: Surveys learning under concept drift, including adaptive algorithms, drift-handling strategies, and evaluation methodology for changing data streams. It provides transfer foundations for longitudinally adapting user-priority models when behavior changes.

title: Mining Sequential Update Summarization with Hierarchical Text Analysis
abstract: Studies sequential update summarization in which successive outputs should contain relevant, novel, timely, and concise information. Its evaluation includes gain, latency, and comprehensiveness measures, providing transfer evidence for longitudinal information selection and omission-sensitive evaluation.

title: Fuzzy user-interest drift detection based recommender systems
abstract: Studies recommender systems that detect changes in user interests and adapt recommendations when those interests drift. The work provides transfer evidence for longitudinal personalization under preference change rather than fixed-profile ranking.
venue: IEEE International Conference on Fuzzy Systems

title: Influence of the physical effort of reminder-setting on strategic offloading of delayed intentions
abstract: Uses preregistered experiments to test how the physical cost of setting reminders affects strategic offloading of delayed intentions, including interactions with memory demands. It contributes evidence about the cost-benefit determinants of whether an outstanding intention is externally supported.

title: Time to Split: Exploring Data Splitting Strategies for Offline Evaluation of Sequential Recommenders
abstract: Compares data-splitting strategies for sequential recommender evaluation and shows that split choice can materially change measured performance and model ordering. It highlights temporal leakage risks and motivates global temporal splits when the goal is future-period behavior.

title: Confidence guides spontaneous cognitive offloading
abstract: Shows that people spontaneously use external reminders more when confidence in unaided memory is lower, even after accounting for objective memory ability. Reminder use improves task performance, providing evidence that subjective forgetting risk influences offloading decisions.

title: Supporting Prospective Information in Email
abstract: Studies email as a repository for prospective information about future actions and events. It links observed email-management behavior to prospective-memory requirements and identifies limitations in conventional email interfaces for managing time-sensitive future work.

title: Strategic reminder setting for time-based intentions: Influence of metacognition, delay length, and cue visibility
abstract: Examines reminder selection for time-based intentions as a function of metacognitive beliefs, delay length, and cue visibility. Reminder use increases under conditions associated with greater prospective-memory difficulty, providing evidence about forgetting-risk signals relevant to content selection.

title: Lexicographically-ordered constraint satisfaction problems
abstract: Formalizes constraint problems in which feasibility constraints and preferences are represented separately and preferences can be ordered lexicographically. It supplies a transferable formal mechanism for obligation-before-preference decision rules.
